rows: Black Bean Aphid	Aphids on leaves	Pinch off infested tips; squash small damaging colonies. Allow natural predators time to act.
Chocolate Spot	Spots on leaves	Remove badly diseased plants. Improve spacing, potash and rotation.
No Pods	Flowers fall without forming pods.	Keep roots moist with mulch and deep watering, especially from flowering.
Pea And Bean Weevil	Notched leaves	Water seedlings in dry spells and protect vulnerable young plants with insect-proof mesh.

Halo Blight	Spots on leaves	Lift and destroy diseased plants. Practise crop rotation. Never soak seed before sowing if halo blight is suspected, never save seed from affected plants, and do not sow beans in the same affected spot the following year.

Bean Seed Fly	Tunnelled seedlings	Destroy damaged seedlings. Prepare a good seed bed or plant compost-raised seedlings.
No Pods	Flowers fail to set pods during drought, heat or poor pollination.	Keep roots moist with mulch and water after flowering.
Halo Blight	Leaves show water-soaked spots surrounded by yellow halos.	Burn plants, save no seed, and avoid the same spot next year.
Slugs	Young plants are chewed, especially in cool, wet weather.	Plant in warm conditions and protect seedlings until vigorous.
Mosaic Disease	Leaves develop yellow blotches and distorted growth.	Pull up and destroy plants; avoid ground recently containing clover.
Birds And Animals	Seeds or young plants disappear or are pulled up.	Raise plants in modules and protect rows with netting.
Bolting	Plants sometimes run to seed before roots have developed.	Avoid very early sowing, thin promptly and choose a bolt-resistant variety.
Fanging	Forked roots are usually caused by adding fresh manure shortly before sowing.	Avoid fresh manure, stones and rough heavy soil; use well-rotted compost.
Mangold Fly (Leaf Miner)	Blistered leaves	Pick off and destroy affected leaves. Treat promptly if damage spreads.
Heart Rot	Blackened roots	Correct confirmed boron deficiency carefully; avoid overdosing.
Blackleg	Blackleg is a serious disease of seedlings, causing them to turn black and shrivel.	Remove diseased plants. Sow thinly and avoid compacted, waterlogged soil.
Carrot Fly	Tunnelled roots	Cover with fine mesh, sow thinly and destroy thinnings. Avoid bruising roots.
Fanging	Forked roots	Remove stones, improve soil deeply and avoid fresh manure.

Small Roots	Aphids and virus will stunt growth and reduce yield, but even in the absence of pests and diseases many gardeners produce disappointingly small carrots.	Improve soil deeply and feed slow plants with a liquid or foliar feed.
Splitting	Split roots	Water deeply and regularly, mulch in drought and use split roots promptly.
Sclerotinia Rot	Mouldy roots	Lift and destroy diseased plants. Store only sound roots and rotate crops.
Slugs	Leaves and seedlings are raggedly chewed, often overnight.	Keep soil clean, patrol at dusk, and use barriers or traps.
Root Aphid	Plants suddenly wilt and die as aphids attack the roots.	Rotate crops and use resistant varieties.
Mildew	Older leaves develop mildew, especially in damp autumn weather.	Pick regularly and improve airflow.
Tipburn	Leaf margins turn brown on large hearting plants in hot, dry weather.	Keep moisture even or grow smaller, regularly picked plants.
Bolting	Lettuces produce thick flowering stems if left in the soil after hearts have formed.	Remove unusable bolted plants and compost them.
Flea Beetle	Seedling leaves are peppered with tiny holes.	Hose plants or protect valuable sowings with mesh or fleece.
Bolting	Plants flower before forming usable roots.	Sow winter radishes from July onwards.
Cabbage Root Fly	Roots are tunnelled by maggots, especially after May sowings.	Use mesh or fleece; trim cosmetic damage from large roots.
Woody Or Hollow Roots	Roots become hot, woody, hollow or soft.	Water evenly, thin well and harvest promptly.
Acid Soil	Plants grow poorly in acid soil.	Apply lime where needed, especially for winter radishes.
